question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's consolidated authority within the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced through ongoing anti-corruption purges in the military and senior ranks through early 2026, underpins trader consensus that he will remain in power through at least the end of 2026. Official proceedings, including the 20th Central Committee's plenums and personnel appointments such as Zhang Shengmin to the Central Military Commission, show no signs of leadership transition ahead of the scheduled 21st Party Congress in late 2027, where a fourth term remains the anticipated outcome. While health rumors and occasional absences have fueled speculation, these lack substantiation from primary sources and align with patterns of unverified claims over prior years. Realistic shifts before 2027 would require abrupt developments such as a verifiable health crisis or unprecedented elite defection, both of which face substantial institutional and surveillance barriers.
